faq.q: Does an easement automatically prevent a house sale?
faq.a: Do not assume that an easement label answers whether your transaction can close. Have the actual document, survey and proposed use reviewed by the appropriate title and legal professionals before promising a result.

faq.q: Is the fence enough to show the easement's location?
faq.a: A fence is an observed improvement, not a substitute for reviewing the easement document and survey. Ask a surveyor about location and a qualified attorney about the legal rights involved.

faq.q: Does a cash offer remove an easement?
faq.a: No. A buyer's cash funding does not itself change another party's rights. The actual title, survey and contract questions still need appropriate review.

faq.q: Should I remove a structure before requesting an offer?
faq.a: Do not act on a guessed location or an assumed requirement. Identify the issue and ask qualified professionals what is needed before budgeting removal or promising changes.
